prose: Google DeepMind launched EmbeddingGemma 2, a 740M-parameter model that natively maps text, code, images, video and audio into one shared embedding space - enabling queries like finding a video clip from a voice memo or searching hours of audio with text, all on-device. It builds on the Gemma 4 architecture, ships under Apache 2.0, and follows the original EmbeddingGemma, which passed 20 million downloads as a lightweight engine for on-device search and privacy-first RAG.

DeepMind claims EmbeddingGemma 2 matches its predecessor's multilingual text performance while jumping 9.92 points on MTEB Code (68.76 to 78.68), making it suitable for local codebase indexing and coding-agent retrieval. Across image, video, documents and audio it sets a new quality-per-parameter standard for sub-1B models, outperforming some specialist models twice its size.
highlights: EmbeddingGemma 2: 740M parameters mapping text, code, images, video and audio into one space.
Apache 2.0 license; built on the Gemma 4 architecture; designed for on-device inference.
Original EmbeddingGemma passed 20M downloads for on-device search and RAG.
MTEB Code score up 9.92 points to 78.68 - aimed at codebase indexing and agent retrieval.
Sets a quality-per-parameter standard for sub-1B multimodal embedding models.
